chunks: From him, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halbi, from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who believe and did not mix their faith with iniquity.' He said: 'With doubt.'
ai.seo_question: What does 'mixing faith with iniquity' mean in Quran 6:82 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the 'iniquity' (zulm) in Quran 6:82 as 'doubt' (shakk), a view supported by the majority of Shia exegetes who distinguish this spiritual doubt from mere uncertainty. This interpretation highlights that while minor doubt may not nullify faith entirely, it diminishes its perfection and purity, serving as a critical criterion for evaluating the sincerity of one's belief.
